input.strategy_title: Graduate Llama Stack to General Availability
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

Llama Stack shipped as Tech Preview and adoption is strong, but enterprise
customers will not build production GenAI applications on a TP component.
Graduating to GA requires API stability commitments, a production support
posture, and closing the quality gaps that TP status currently excuses. The
full inventory of those gaps is not yet known — TP feedback is scattered across
support tickets, and no systematic GA-readiness assessment has been done.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | A GA-readiness assessment inventories the gaps between current TP quality and GA bar (API stability, upgrade paths, scale limits, error handling), producing the definitive GA scope. |
| HLR-2 | P0 | Published API surface carries a stability guarantee: versioned APIs, deprecation policy, and a tested upgrade path from the last two TP releases. |
| HLR-3 | P0 | Production support posture is in place: documented SLO targets, backport policy, and supported configuration matrix. |
| HLR-4 | P1 | Safety guardrails via TrustyAI are a supported, documented integration (not an experimental flag) for GA distributions. |
| HLR-5 | P1 | The Dashboard enables Llama Stack management by default for entitled clusters (no TP opt-in gate). |
| HLR-6 | P2 | Documentation is uplifted to GA standards, including migration notes from TP. |

## Affected Components

- Llama Stack
- TrustyAI
- Dashboard

## Out of Scope

- New Llama Stack feature development beyond GA-bar quality work
- Deprecating alternative GenAI serving paths

## Open Questions

1. The GA scope itself depends on HLR-1's assessment — until it lands, the
   size of the stability and hardening work is an estimate.

# GA-Readiness Assessment for Llama Stack

## Description

Resolves the strategy's defining unknown: no systematic GA-readiness assessment of Llama Stack has been done, and the full inventory of gaps that Tech Preview status currently excuses is not known. This investigation inventories the gaps between current TP quality and the GA bar across API stability, upgrade paths, scale limits, and error handling, and produces the definitive GA scope that all downstream Llama Stack graduation work is planned against.

## Scope

- Define the GA-bar evaluation dimensions per the strategy: API stability, upgrade paths, scale limits, error handling.
- Audit the current Tech Preview state against each dimension, using the component's upstream and midstream source repositories, the platform distribution, and the TP feedback scattered across support tickets.
- Consolidate TP feedback from support tickets and map each item to a gap area.
- Produce a gap inventory that states, per gap: current state, GA bar, severity, and remediation sizing.
- Identify which gaps change the scope or approach of the API stability work, the quality remediation work, and the production support posture work.
- Output the definitive GA scope document, accepted by the owning team and product stakeholders as the basis for the graduation work.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The gap inventory covers all four dimensions (API stability, upgrade paths, scale limits, error handling), with current state, GA bar, and gap recorded per item.
- TP feedback from support tickets is consolidated and mapped to inventory items.
- Each inventory item is classified by whether it affects the scope or approach of the stability, remediation, or support-posture work, so downstream scope can be finalized from the inventory alone.
- The resulting GA scope document is reviewed and accepted by the owning team and the product stakeholder as the definitive GA scope.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): directly delivers the GA-readiness assessment that inventories the gaps between current TP quality and the GA bar and produces the definitive GA scope.

# API Stability Guarantee and Tested Upgrade Path

## Description

Puts a stability guarantee on the published Llama Stack API surface so enterprise customers can build production GenAI applications against it: versioned APIs, a published deprecation policy, and a tested upgrade path from the last two Tech Preview releases. The scope of stability hardening is finalized from the GA-readiness assessment's API-stability gap inventory.

## Scope

- Introduce API versioning on the published API surface of the platform's Llama Stack distribution.
- Publish a deprecation policy stating what stability guarantee the versioned surface carries and how breaking changes are handled.
- Implement and verify an upgrade path from each of the last two Tech Preview releases to the GA release.
- Remediate the API-stability gap items that the GA-readiness assessment assigns to this surface.
- Keep the versioned surface consistent with the surfaces consumed by the platform's Llama Stack integrations (guardrails integration, Dashboard management) so the stability guarantee applies to them.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The published API surface is versioned and the versioning is visible to API consumers.
- A deprecation policy is published and covers the versioned API surface.
- Upgrade from each of the last two Tech Preview releases to the GA candidate is executed and verified in a test environment, with failures remediated.
- All API-stability gap items from the GA-readiness assessment assigned to this surface are closed or explicitly deferred with accepted rationale.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P0): published API surface carries a stability guarantee — versioned APIs, deprecation policy, and a tested upgrade path from the last two TP releases.

# GA Quality Gap Remediation

## Description

Closes the quality gaps that the GA-readiness assessment inventories — beyond API stability — bringing Llama Stack from Tech Preview quality to the GA bar. The epic's scope is defined by the assessment's gap inventory: scale limits, error handling, and any other TP-era quality excusals it identifies.

## Scope

- Remediate the assessed gap items across scale limits, error handling, and the other quality dimensions in the GA-readiness assessment's inventory; every remediation item traces to an inventoried gap.
- Characterize scale limits to the level needed to define the supported configuration matrix consumed by the production support posture work.
- Raise error handling to the GA bar defined by the assessment.
- Verify no regression in the capabilities the platform's Llama Stack integrations rely on.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Every gap item in the assessment's inventory assigned to quality remediation is closed, or explicitly deferred with rationale accepted by the product stakeholder.
- Error handling meets the GA bar defined by the assessment.
- Scale limits are characterized and handed off in a form the supported configuration matrix can consume.
- The remediation introduces no regression in existing TP functionality.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): closes the gaps the GA-readiness assessment inventories, delivering the GA-bar quality the HLR requires (assessment half covered by the investigation epic).

# Production Support Posture

## Description

Establishes the production support posture required for GA: documented SLO targets, a backport policy, and a supported configuration matrix. Enterprise customers will not run production workloads without these commitments; their content is finalized from the GA-readiness assessment's findings (scale limits, error handling, supported configurations).

## Scope

- Define and document SLO targets for the GA Llama Stack distribution.
- Define the backport policy: which release lines receive fixes and for how long.
- Define the supported configuration matrix — supported deployment configurations, dependency versions, and the scale limits characterized by the GA quality remediation work.
- Publish the support posture as product support documentation, reflecting all findings from the GA-readiness assessment that bear on supportability.

## Acceptance Criteria

- SLO targets are documented and approved by product and support stakeholders.
- The backport policy is documented and approved.
- The supported configuration matrix is published and incorporates the characterized scale limits and the assessed supported configurations.
- The published support posture reflects the GA-readiness assessment's findings (no assessed supportability gap is left unaddressed or undocumented).

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-3 (P0): production support posture in place — documented SLO targets, backport policy, and supported configuration matrix.

# TrustyAI Guardrails as a Supported Integration

## Description

Promotes safety guardrails via TrustyAI for Llama Stack from an experimental flag to a supported integration for GA distributions. The TrustyAI guardrails capability itself is already GA in the platform; this epic makes its integration with Llama Stack distributions a supported and validated part of the GA offering. The integration documentation (usage, configuration, and support boundaries) is authored in the GA documentation uplift; this epic supplies the technical input for that content.

## Scope

- Move the TrustyAI guardrails integration for Llama Stack distributions from experimental/opt-in gating to supported status.
- Validate the integration to supported status: functional coverage, failure behavior, and supported configurations.
- Provide the technical input for the integration documentation — usage, configuration, and support boundaries — that the GA documentation uplift authors and publishes. Authorship is not part of this epic; content authoring and code implementation have different review criteria and belong in separate epics.
- Validate the integration against the versioned Llama Stack API surface that carries the stability guarantee, so the surfaces it consumes are covered by that guarantee.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The guardrails integration is available as supported (not gated behind an experimental flag) in GA Llama Stack distributions.
- Validation covers the integration's functional surface and its failure behavior.
- Technical input for the integration documentation (usage, configuration, and support boundaries) is complete and handed off to the GA documentation uplift.
- The integration is validated against the versioned Llama Stack API surface carrying the stability guarantee.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-4 (P1): safety guardrails via TrustyAI are a supported, documented integration (not an experimental flag) for GA distributions. This epic delivers the supported, validated integration and the removal of the experimental gate; the documentation half of HLR-4 is authored in the GA documentation uplift with technical input from this epic.

# Dashboard Llama Stack Management Enabled by Default

## Description

The Dashboard enables Llama Stack management by default for entitled clusters, removing the Tech Preview opt-in gate. Llama Stack management surfaces (navigation, resource views, and management flows) become part of the default Dashboard experience wherever the cluster is entitled.

## Scope

- Change the Dashboard's Llama Stack management enablement from Tech Preview opt-in to default-on for entitled clusters.
- Keep non-entitled clusters unchanged: management surfaces remain hidden where there is no entitlement.
- Preserve a configuration path to disable the enablement (rollback path), consistent with the Dashboard's per-component feature-flag and defaults mechanism.
- Update captions, labels, and references that still describe Llama Stack management as Tech Preview as part of the same change (incidental touch-ups, no new content).

## Acceptance Criteria

- On an entitled cluster with default Dashboard configuration, Llama Stack management surfaces are available without any opt-in action.
- On a non-entitled cluster, Llama Stack management surfaces remain hidden.
- The enablement can be disabled through Dashboard configuration without code rollback.
- Existing opt-in users see no regression in their management flows when the default flips.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-5 (P1): the Dashboard enables Llama Stack management by default for entitled clusters (no TP opt-in gate).

# GA Documentation Uplift with TP Migration Notes

## Description

Uplifts Llama Stack documentation to GA standards, including migration notes from Tech Preview. The documentation describes the GA behavior that was actually built: the versioned API surface and tested upgrade path, the production support posture, and default Dashboard enablement. This epic also authors the documentation for the supported TrustyAI guardrails integration — usage, configuration, and support boundaries — with technical input from the guardrails work.

## Scope

Content outline:

- GA-standard documentation for Llama Stack: installation, configuration, supported usage, and the supported deployment configurations from the support posture.
- Migration notes from Tech Preview releases to GA, aligned with the tested upgrade path from the last two TP releases.
- Documentation of the GA support posture: SLO targets, backport policy, and the supported configuration matrix.
- Documentation of the supported TrustyAI guardrails integration — usage, configuration, and support boundaries, to the level required for a supported GA integration — authored here with technical input from the guardrails work, and documentation of the default Dashboard enablement for entitled clusters.
- Technical review of all new and changed content against the implemented GA behavior.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Documentation meets GA documentation standards for the component.
- Migration notes cover the TP releases from which the upgrade path is tested.
